description:
Implement and evaluate a HIP/ROCm batch LDPC normalized min-sum belief-propagation prototype.

## Background

LDPC BP dominates decoding time in coded simulation campaigns. The prototype batches frames on GPU while preserving CPU/GPU correctness and comparing against the best current production CPU path at the same workload shape, including rayon where production uses rayon.

Existing design doc: `dev/active/gpu-batch-ldpc-bp-plan.md`. Epic spec: `dev/plans/hip_gpu_prototype_wave.md`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] `GpuLdpcGraph` correctly represents CPU sparse parity-check structure, including edge counts, check/variable offsets, and mate indices consistent with CPU row/column iterators.
- [hard] HIP kernels implement check-node normalized min-sum, variable-node update, and syndrome or early-termination support with deterministic host-side orchestration.
- [hard] Safe Rust wrappers in `gf2-kernels-hip` and feature-gated `gf2-coding` integration compile only behind the `hip` feature; default workspace builds succeed without ROCm installed.
- [hard] CPU/GPU correctness fixtures cover Hamming, 5G NR BG2, and DVB-T2 short Rate1/2; hard decisions match exactly where specified and LLR/belief differences stay within documented tolerances.
- [hard] Batch correctness covers the selected design workload and at least one smaller fixture; GPU batch output matches CPU serial/batch comparator semantics.
- [hard] Early termination converges before `max_iterations` on high-SNR noiseless inputs and matches CPU convergence behavior where the CPU path exposes the same criterion.
- [hard] Performance evidence records hardware metadata, ROCm version, benchmark command, raw result paths, batch-size sweep, and phase timing where practical.
- [hard] GPU LDPC BP is at least 3x faster than the best existing production CPU path at the selected design workload.

## Notes

Target environment: AMD RX 6950 XT / `gfx1030`, ROCm 7.2, `/opt/rocm/bin/hipcc`. Do not compare only against an artificially serial CPU loop unless the best production CPU path is also reported and used for the hard speed criterion.
